newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Uninspired Dutch money market unmoved, call down.
newsitem.headline: Uninspired Dutch money market unmoved, call down.

text.p: Dutch call money lost some ground to return to Thursday's level on Monday in thin trade.
Call money was bid 2.75 percent, 0.06 percent lower than on Friday, and was said to change hands at 2.88 percent, down from Friday's 2.93 percent.

Dealers said the slight drop in call rates could be interpreted as a sign that last week's allocation under the special advances pact had been sufficient, adding the usual upward pressure ahead of the week-end was also gone.
Trade focused on overnight money and on short-dated deposits as market players, not knowing what direction interest rates are heading, preferring to remain close to home.
Payments of the newly issued ten-year benchmark did not move money market rates, dealers said.
"That was all already included in rates," one dealer said.
Dealers said trade was extremely thin as the market lacked inspiration.
"My prices for one-month deposits are the same as two weeks ago. We need some real changes in for instance the German repo in order to wake things up over here," one dealer said.
He said today's closure of the American market added to the market's lethargy.
"Normally, we readjust our price levels in the afternoon, watching the U.S., and we also get some American orders," he said.
"Today, the story about the Dutch money market is more on what does not happen than on what does happen."
The guilder was virtually unchanged against the mark, trading at 112.251 per 100 marks versus 112.25 on Friday.
